clue.text: Elders perhaps encourage branch manager?

parts.note: elders are a kind of tree, so 'perhaps' marks them as an example of trees
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: A query about whether older staff might motivate the manager of a bank branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branch manager' reads as an office title, but the branches are those of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a specialist who prunes and tends the boughs of trees literally manages branches.

clue.text: News can be so old, writing after an interval

indicators.note: the writing comes after the interval

parts.note: a third is a musical interval
hand is handwriting

explanation.surface: News may be stale: written up some time after it happened.
explanation.definitionFit: Information passed through several intermediaries is described as at third hand, i.e. not first-hand.

clue.text: Pedal attachment picked up outside shed light on early tools

indicators.note: the reversed footwear goes outside the lighting word
in a down clue, picked up means read from the bottom up

parts.note: a shoe is attached to a foot, a pedal extremity
lit means shed light on

explanation.surface: A cycling accessory raised to illuminate primitive stone implements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedal' suggests a bicycle; it means of the foot. 'picked up' turns SHOE into EOHS, which goes 'outside' LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eoliths are crudely chipped flints thought to be the earliest stone implements.

clue.text: Great bird that hunts big game

parts.note: superb means great
an owl is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A fine bird of prey that hunts large animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big game' suggests hunting, but it is the American football championship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Super Bowl is American football's championship final, the biggest game of the season.

clue.text: Irritable Republican lawyer getting short

parts.note: an attorney is a lawyer, and ATTY is its shortened form

explanation.surface: A cranky Republican lawyer snapping at people.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: someone ratty is irritable and bad-tempered.

clue.text: English politician getting no publicity set up large-scale marketing operations

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
O is nought, none

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means written upwards

parts.note: airtime, or air, is publicity

explanation.surface: An English MP, starved of publicity, launches big marketing ventures.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia are large shops or trading centres, places where marketing on a big scale happens.

clue.text: Broadcast controlled by Nationalists in Scottish town

indicators.note: being controlled by means held between them

parts.note: N is short for Nationalist, doubled for the plural
to air something is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Broadcasting in a Scottish town is run by the SNP.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairn is a town on the Moray Firth in the Highlands of Scotland.

clue.text: Language in Africa both sides spin

parts.note: Twi is a language spoken in Ghana
the two sides are right and left, abbreviated R and L

explanation.surface: Someone describing an African language whose spin puts both sides of a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to spin round is to rotate or whirl on the spot.

clue.text: Transport czar's illegal activity

parts.note: traffic is transport, the movement of vehicles
a czar is a Russian king

explanation.surface: A transport supremo turns out to be doing something criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Trafficking is illegal dealing in goods such as drugs or people.

clue.text: Bear market — hard to gather intelligence

indicators.note: the hard letter is collected on to the end of the word for intelligence

parts.note: to put up goods for sale is to market them
wit is mental sharpness or intelligence
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A bear market, where it is difficult to gather market intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear market' looks like one stock-exchange phrase, but 'Bear' is the definition and 'market' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to bear something is to tolerate or endure it.

clue.text: Greeting observed by church in which minister's introduced the Cardinal

parts.note: hi is a greeting

indicators.note: the minister is brought into the words for observed and church

parts.note: seen means observed
MIN is short for minister, with 's as 'is'
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A cardinal arrives at a church service, greeted and watched as a minister introduces him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greeting' and 'church' suggest a service; 'introduced' signals insertion. His Eminence is the formal style for a Catholic cardinal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal is addressed by the honorific title His Eminence.

clue.text: Finance officer gets motor trip that's not for everyone

parts.note: an Audi is a make of car, a motor

indicators.note: U is the film rating meaning suitable for everyone, so this phrase drops that letter

parts.note: a tour is a trip

explanation.surface: An accounts officer is given a car and an exclusive excursion.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film classification 'universal', for all ages; removing it from TOUR leaves TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: one who examines financial accounts officially is a finance officer of a kind.

clue.text: Mrs Piggy's picked up underwear

indicators.note: picked up by the ear, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: Mrs is a wife, and the piggy of a litter is its runt, so the phrase becomes wife-runts

explanation.surface: Miss Piggy's married counterpart's things, heard about, turn out to be underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: A runt is the smallest pig in a litter. Spoken quickly, 'wife runts' gives the name of the men's briefs with a Y-shaped front opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Y-fronts are a style of men's briefs, so they are an item of underwear.

clue.text: From recitation, expression gets worn out

indicators.note: recitation is speaking aloud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a phrase is an expression

explanation.surface: Someone saying a stock expression so often that it becomes worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: fabric that frays is worn ragged at the edges.

clue.text: East German xenophobia gets cold shoulder

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east
hostility to foreigners is a form of racism

explanation.surface: A news line: xenophobia in eastern Germany leads to people being shunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' looks like a person from the old GDR; it is the German word for east.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: deliberately excluding someone from a group is giving them the cold shoulder.

clue.text: It's displayed in bed, dear toy losing stuffing?

definitions.text: It's displayed in bed, dear toy losing stuffing?

indicators.note: displayed suggests the letters set out anew, rearranged
stuffing is the middle letter of the word, which is removed

explanation.surface: A child's soft toy, kept on the bed and losing its filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing stuffing' takes the middle O from TOY, leaving TY; BED, DEAR and TY are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuddly toy bear is the thing commonly propped on a bed and liable to lose its stuffing.

clue.text: Make a fool of, reportedly, through your consumption of butter

indicators.note: reported speech, so the phrase is heard

parts.note: through gives IN, butter is a fat, and your consumption is you ate

explanation.surface: Someone fooled into thinking butter consumption is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: To infatuate is to inspire foolish passion in someone, making a fool of them.

clue.text: Clubbed together, perhaps, after something having been chewed over

indicators.note: the word for coming together follows the chewed thing

parts.note: cud is food a cow brings up and chews again
things that have gelled have come together

explanation.surface: A group pooled resources, maybe, after much deliberation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubbed together' reads as pooling money; 'Clubbed' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to be beaten with a heavy stick is to be clubbed.

clue.text: Orient's sweeper's centre back

indicators.note: the centre of the seven-letter word is its fourth letter

parts.note: astern means at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A football report on Leyton Orient's sweeper playing at centre back.
explanation.walkthrough: Leyton Orient is a London football club; a sweeper and centre back are defensive positions. Here 'Orient's' is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the Orient means belonging to the East, the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Sweet Malaga's the ultimate

definitions.meaning: sweet in the sense of small, dainty and charming

explanation.surface: A wine buff calling sweet Malaga wine the very best.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin features are delicate and charming, i.e. sweet; and in Spanish the phrase means the end.

clue.text: Uncovered workstation worker's to have a spell on

indicators.note: the top of the down entry is uncovered, its first letter removed

parts.note: a bench is a worktable
worker ant is the usual crossword ant

explanation.surface: A worker stripped of their workstation gets a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' takes off only the top letter, B, here.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant is to bewitch, to cast a spell over someone.

clue.text: Pushes setter's attitudes

parts.note: the setter is 'I', and 'setter's' stands for I'M, setter is
poses are attitudes or postures

explanation.surface: Someone forcing the crossword setter's opinions on others.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to impose something is to force or push it on others.

clue.text: Source of e.g. drama you get in instalments?

definitions.text: Source of e.g. drama you get in instalments?

parts.words: Source of e.g. drama you get in instalments?
parts.note: a drama series arrives in episodes, but the joke is that you also pay for the subscription by instalments

explanation.surface: A viewer watching a drama series episode by episode.
explanation.definitionFit: Subscription television is paid for in regular payments and serves up drama in episodes.

clue.text: Genre producing audible sounds of dejection and disgust

indicators.note: audible means the words are heard said

parts.note: a sigh shows dejection and fie shows disgust

explanation.surface: A literary form that leaves readers sighing and groaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction is a category of fiction and film, a genre.

clue.text: Chinese money cornering tortoiseshell perhaps in area of Mexico

indicators.note: the money corners, or encloses, the animal

parts.note: the yuan is the currency of China
a tortoiseshell is a type of cat

explanation.surface: Chinese investors buying up tortoiseshell goods in a part of Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tortoiseshell' suggests the material; here it is the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Yucatan peninsula is a region of south-eastern Mexico.

clue.text: Alcohol has Young Conservatives reeling merrily

indicators.note: a merry, tipsy mixing up of the letters

parts.note: YC is short for Young Conservatives

explanation.surface: Young party members, drunk, staggering about happily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alcohol' suggests drink; it is meant in the chemist's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry: glycerine is a trihydric alcohol, so it counts as an alcohol.

clue.text: Commercial will take a very long time — say it again and again!

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: An exasperated complaint that a commercial runs too long and is repeated endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: An old saying is something people repeat endlessly, hence 'say it again and again!'

clue.text: Integrative reforms that will be put on the table in France

definitions.text: that will be put on the table in France

indicators.note: reforms means the letters are formed again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Political reforms that will be tabled in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on the table' suggests a proposal being tabled; it is a dressing served at a French table.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinaigrette is the classic French salad dressing, something placed on the dinner table.
